brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A green tea from Jian'ou in Fujian, described as steamed and ground to paste, today sold mostly loose with some brick and cake forms. Its name recalls the imperial tribute gardens of Beiyuan.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: Tribute production is said to have begun in the Tang and peaked in the Song, running through the Min, Song, Yuan and Ming for 458 years. Imperial works called dragon kilns were set up at Beiyuan in old Jian'an, now Jian'ou, with envoys sent to oversee them.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Tight, heavy strips with an oily, dark sandy green colour.
appearance_wet: Thick, soft, bright yellow leaves with reddish edges.
taste_profile: Rich, lasting orchid-like aroma and a mellow taste with a sweet return.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
